summary.name: Map (Wikipedia article)
summary.one_liner: A Wikipedia article covering maps in cartography: their definition, uses, history, and design principles such as scale, generalization, symbolization, and projection.
use_cases: background on GIS and digital mapping
summary.what_it_does: The article defines a map as a representation or abstraction of geographic reality and lists its uses in navigation, science, government, military, and public health. It traces map history from a 2300 BCE clay tablet and Ptolemy's world map through the Age of Discovery, thematic maps, the 20th-century shift to computer cartography and GIS, and modern phone map apps. It explains map design topics: visual hierarchy, basemaps, neatlines, scale ratios and resolution, generalization steps, symbolization, and projections. The page is descriptive and does not sell a product.
notable: Covers the history of maps from ancient clay tablets to digital GIS
Explains map scale, resolution, and generalization in detail
Describes how projections introduce unavoidable distortion
caveats: Reference article, not a software tool; the listing's awesome-selfhosted context does not apply to the page content
Excerpt ends mid-section on projections, so later sections were not read
